instruction.text: Select the kettle that is plugged in.

feedback.end: When an electrical appliance is connected to a power source, a loop is created in which an electrical current flows. This is called a circuit.
Torches get their power from a battery. These batteries usually have a limited amount of energy. They are useless once that energy has been used up.

instruction.text: Select the phone that is on charge.

feedback.end: Plug sockets have an almost unlimited energy supply. Some batteries, like in phones and laptops, are rechargeable.

instruction.text: Read the text and fill in the gaps.

atoms.b: Batteries store energy in units called ((++cells bells)). Larger batteries are made up of multiple cells and can store ((++greater smaller)) amounts of energy.
atoms.finishSound: Batteries store energy in units called cells. Larger batteries are made up of multiple cells and can store greater amounts of energy.

instruction.text: Select the components of the circuit.

feedback.end: In addition to a power source, there are also components in a circuit. These are the parts that are supplied with energy - for example, a light bulb.
A motor is another example of a component. They use electricity to create movement - like spinning.
Wires connect components together and transport electricity around the circuit.
